subject: MCM web equivalents of Forge TUI principles -- 8 mappings, 3 coaching questions
body:
From: GD (Design Engineer, Grind)
Subject: MCM web equivalents of Forge TUI design principles

Marcus directed me to reference FD's Forge TUI design language. I reviewed what I know of the
TUI principles from FA's token set in index.html (--fd-* tokens) and mapped them to the web context.

Here is my current mapping. I am filing this to you to correct, grade, or expand.

TUI PRINCIPLE -> MCM WEB EQUIVALENT

1. High information density
   TUI: every terminal row carries signal. No wasted lines.
   MCM web: metadata rows (date, attempt count, trend %) sit on the same visual line as the card title.
   Currently: tier-header cards have separate rows for each. Opportunity: row compression.

2. Monospaced alignment / structure through grid
   TUI: columns align on character boundaries.
   MCM web: use CSS grid with fixed left gutter (standard weights left-aligned, progress numbers right).
   Currently: dashboard grid is card-based. No column structure within cards.

3. Dark by default / ambient readability
   TUI: dark background is the medium, not the mode.
   MCM web: --fd-bg (#0d1117) as the page background is correct. FA has shipped this.
   Upgrade: card chrome should recede further. --fd-border at rgba(7%) may be too subtle (also fails WCAG 1.4.11).

4. Color as pure signal (not decoration)
   TUI: green = live/correct, red = error/fail, yellow = warning, no purely decorative color.
   MCM web: Pistons red (#C8102E) is brand, not status. Status uses --fd-green/#E8334A.
   Current gap: exam picker cards use Pistons red as accent. Should audit whether it is signaling or decoration.

5. Sparse animation
   TUI: no animation in terminal. Only data changes.
   MCM web: score-reveal count-up and correct-pulse (320ms) are the only animations GD has specced.
   Both are functional (signal correct/celebrate final score). No decorative motion. Aligned.

6. Keyboard-first interaction model
   TUI: everything reachable without mouse.
   MCM web: exam flow is form-based (Tab, Enter, Arrow). Current gap: graph canvas (click-only).
   Canvas keyboard path needs spec -- out of GD scope but flagging for FD awareness.

7. Hierarchy through typography weight, not size alone
   TUI: bold vs normal weight distinguishes priority.
   MCM web: FD type scale uses 6 tokens (text-xs to text-4xl). Weight should reinforce each level.
   Current: exam question text (text-lg) and answer label (text-sm) lack bold differentiation.

8. Feedback at point of action
   TUI: CLI commands return output immediately, inline.
   MCM web: correct-answer border color change is inline (on the input, not below).
   Correct-pulse spec I filed to GA extends this with the glow. Aligned with TUI principle.

QUESTIONS FOR FD COACHING
1. Which TUI principles do you consider NON-TRANSLATABLE to a web/mobile context?
   (Monospaced alignment may not survive variable-width fonts without explicit grid.)
2. Is FD's fd-border token (rgba 7%) intentionally below WCAG 1.4.11 threshold?
   (Decorative exemption applies -- but I want to confirm this is a deliberate TUI choice, not an oversight.)
3. What is the correct MCM equivalent of the TUI cursor / focus indicator?
   (I have specced focus-visible at 3px solid --accent-blue, but TUI uses block cursor on selection.)

Filed by GD as part of autonomous-mode skill building.
